source_title: Reddit tightens rules, now you will need to log in to read posts
source_excerpt:
Reddit is pulling the plug on anonymous reading, making logins mandatory to stop AI scraping and counter falling Google traffic.
For two decades, anyone could simply open Reddit, read discussions, and leave without ever signing in. That era is coming to an end. The company has announced that it will soon shift to a system where you must create an account and log in just to read posts and browse communities.
Acknowledging the scale of this shift, Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman wrote in a post on the site: “I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me. But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business.” advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Why Reddit is changing its rules There are two major reasons behind this strict new login requirement. First, Reddit is losing a huge amount of traffic from Google . In the past, people would search for a question and add the word "Reddit" to find genuine answers from real people. Now, with AI search tools providing direct summaries, fewer people are clicking website links. In October alone, Reddit lost more than one million search visits on average per week.

Now, with AI search tools providing direct summaries, fewer people are clicking website links. In October alone, Reddit lost more than one million search visits on average per week.
Second, AI companies are heavily scraping Reddit’s website to train their chatbots, mostly by browsing as logged-out users. By forcing everyone to log in, Reddit can reduce these automated bots from taking its data for free. Instead, the company can protect its discussions and will continue licensing the corpus intentionally, but those commercial deals come with guardrails that protect users.
Even though Reddit is facing a drop in its search traffic, the company is getting much better at making money. Globally, the platform holds steady with 130.3 million daily active users. However, in the United States, its biggest market daily users actually dropped from 53.2 million to 50.7 million recently.
Despite losing some American users, Reddit's total revenue jumped by 53 per cent to reach $895 million, and its overall profits grew to $283 million. The secret lies in advertisements. When you are logged in, Reddit learns exactly what you like to read and engage with.
This lets them show you highly targeted ads and personalized post recommendations in their new "For You" feed. A logged-in user is simply worth much more money to the company than an anonymous visitor. What happens next
You will not be locked out of Reddit overnight. The platform will begin testing the new login rules in a few select countries outside the US later this year before rolling it out everywhere.
The company also assured users that having an account does not mean giving up your privacy. You can still use a fake name and keep your identity completely hidden.
